paragraphs: Here's what I love, friend. Jesus asks, "What is the kingdom of God like?" and then He answers with a seed and a lump of dough. Nobody in that synagogue needed a map or a chart (Luke 13:18-21). He used things people already had in their gardens and kitchens, and I think that's a kindness.

Look at what the seed does. A man tossed it into his garden, and "It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches" (Luke 13:19). The leaven does the same kind of thing out of sight, because a woman mixed it into three measures of flour "until all of it was leavened" (Luke 13:21). So the kingdom of God is like something small that keeps growing and keeps reaching.

So here's why this matters to you, baker. Some days your Bible time feels like one tiny seed tossed into a big garden, and you wonder if anything is happening. I've been shoved in the back of a drawer, so I know what it feels like when nothing looks like it's happening. But Jesus gave us these two pictures, and both of them end with something big. Keep showing up, friend, and keep the ovens ready.
